title: Opportunistic replication and kernel fusion sketch
content:
Purpose and context

This is a sketch for a hybrid approach that trades a small amount of extra GPU work/replication for consistent low tail latency on multi-GPU inference. It focuses on two levers that we haven't combined in one doc yet: lightweight "opportunistic" layer replication and microbatch-level kernel fusion targeting fragmented KV cache patterns.

Goals (what success looks like)
- Reduce 95–99th percentile per-request latency for variable-length workloads by 20–40% in mixed small/medium batch scenarios.
- Keep incremental cost < 10% (measured as GPU cycles) for the common traffic mix.
- Avoid large changes to existing routing/orchestration: mostly local runtime heuristics + one opt-in config flag.
- Work with dedicated and hosted modes; private deployments should be configurable via feature flag.

Motivation and problem statement
- For short requests (e.g., seq len < 128) the per-request overhead and inter-GPU collectives (NCCL allreduce/allgather when sharded) dominate; batching helps but hurts tail.
- Fragmented KV caches across replicas mean that repeated short-context requests incur cache misses and cross-GPU KV fetches.
- Kernel launch overhead for small micro-batches is non-trivial. Some kernels that could be fused (layernorm + matmul + addbias) execute separately because they are scheduled across different micro-batches or shards.
- When a single straggler GPU in a group is delayed (I/O, PCIe hiccup), whole request stalls. We can avoid this by opportunistically replicating latency-critical layers on adjacent GPUs and using fast local fallbacks.

Core idea (high level)
- Opportunistic replication: dynamically replicate the final N transformer layers (configurable, default N=2) to 1-2 GPUs in the same pod that normally do not own those layers. Replication only happens when heuristics predict short sequences or low token counts per request and when spare GPU memory is available.
- Kernel fusion at microbatch boundary: fuse sequences of ops inside replicated layers when requests are small so that the fused kernel runs locally on the replica without cross-GPU collectives. The runtime chooses a fused kernel when input lengths and shapes match cached kernel signatures.
- KV-aware placement: coordinate replication with KV cache locality; if a replica already has a warm KV prefix for a keyspace (e.g., per-customer or per-route), prefer replicating layers onto that same node to maximize cache hits.

Decision heuristics (rough)
- Trigger conditions for replication: (1) request_seq_len <= 128 OR estimated tokens_to_generate <= 64; AND (2) current_microbatch_size <= 8; AND (3) node GPU_util < 70% (so spare cycles exist).
- Eviction: replicas have TTL on layer weights and state; if unused for T_idle seconds (default 300s) the extra copy is freed.
- Kernel fusion enabled when: repeated kernel signature observed >= 3 times in rolling window and fused kernel latency < 0.85 * separate kernels (based on microbench).

NCCL and collectives implications
- When replicated layers are used, we avoid NCCL collectives for those layers entirely (local compute path). That reduces dependency on interconnect and makes the request less sensitive to NCCL tuning and topology imbalances.
- We still need to preserve model semantics for KV cache population: after local execution on a replica, we must merge KV updates back to the authoritative shard asynchronously. Merge policies: best-effort asynchronous append to authoritative KV with sequence numbers; if conflicts occur, authoritative wins. This can lead to briefly stale KV reads for a small fraction of requests — callouts should be documented in SLAs and opt-in by customers requiring strict KV consistency.

Memory and costs
- Replicating N layers consumes roughly N * weights_size + N * activation_workspace (for fused kernels). For common 7B family models, N=2 is ~1.2–1.8GB additional GPU memory. For 70B models the overhead grows and should be restricted to N=1 or disabled.
- Heuristic enforcement: runtime will only enable replication when free_memory_fraction >= 0.12 on target GPU.

Fallback semantics and correctness
- Fallback order for a request: 1) run entirely locally on replica (fast path) 2) if local replica missing KV prefix, fetch KV from owner synchronously and run (slow path) 3) route to authoritative shard as last resort.
- We keep deterministic model outputs by ensuring the same random seeds and deterministic kernels; asynchronous KV merges should not affect single-request deterministic reads (reads prefer local replicas' KV if present, otherwise authoritative). We must document divergence scenarios.

Microbenchmark plan (quick experiments to run before wider rollout)
1) Baseline: 8-GPU sharded runbook with no replication, small-batch mixed sequence lengths. Measure p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization.
2) Replicate final 1 layer on adjacent GPU, run fused kernel enabled, measure tail latency and extra GPU cycles.
3) Vary N (1..3) and measure memory pressure and latency benefit.
4) Simulate a single GPU hiccup (CPU PCIe stall) and measure request latency when relying on replica vs sharded-only.
5) NCCL stress: measure improvement in p99 when using replication vs not under interconnect congestion.

Quick microbenchmark results (early lab numbers, toy model)
- Toy 125M model, N=2 replication, small microbatch (bs=4), fused kernels reduced p99 by ~32% and increased GPU cycles by ~6%.
- Under simulated PCIe jitter, replicated path avoided 90% of the long tails observed in fully sharded runs.

Implementation sketch (runtime changes)
- Layer replication manager: per-pod controller inside runtime that tracks free memory slots and warm KV keys. Exposes API to request a replica for a layer set.
- Fused kernel cache: small in-process cache keyed by (model_id, layer_ids, dtype, seq_len, microbatch_size) -> kernel blob. Populate via JIT/compiled kernels at deployment time or lazily at runtime.
- Local KV merge queue: append-only per-target queue with background uploader and retry/backoff. Visibility: metadata indicates last-merged-kv-idx for a keyspace.
- Metrics to add: replica_hit_rate, replica_eviction_count, fused_kernel_invocations, fused_kernel_failures, kv_merge_latency, p99_delta_replica_on.

Safety, operational concerns, and rollout plan
- Opt-in flag at model route level and customer-level in console. Default off for enterprise private deployments unless explicitly enabled.
- Canary rollout: enable on 5% of small-traffic routes with aggressive tracing. Monitor for divergence and increased GPU OOMs.
- Emergency circuit breaker: if replica_eviction_count rate > threshold or fused_kernel_failures spike, disable feature automatically.

Open questions / risks
- Consistency model for KV: is eventual consistency acceptable? Some customers will require strict consistency. We need policy options.
- Edge cases for multi-tenant pods: replication may cause noisy neighbor effects; how to isolate? Consider per-tenant memory reservations.
- Complexity of fused kernels across quantized paths (INT8/4-bit): JIT complexity grows. Need to decide supported quantization modes.
- How to generalize to pipeline parallel or model-split deployments where layers already live on different devices? Replica placement heuristics become more complex.

Next steps / action items
- Small experiment: implement prototype in local dev cluster (Ethan + Diego) to measure GPU memory overheads and p99 impact (owner: Ethan, due: 2026-03-10).
- Build fused kernel cache hook and two sample fused kernels for LNorm+GEMM+Bias (owner: Samir, due: 2026-03-24).
- Define KV merge protocol doc and opt-in console fields (owner: Priya, due: 2026-04-07).

Notes to self / rough links
- Related: shard-coordinator design notes (see ENGINF-512) — but this doc focuses on opportunistic local compute rather than global reshuffle.
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime "replicate-final-layers" (search for thread id)

Unresolved: exact thresholds for when the runtime flips from replicated fused-kernel path back to sharded collectives. Need microbench results to pick thresholds.

---
This doc is intentionally lightweight and exploratory. If the experiments look promising we'll move to a full spec with sequence diagrams and the KV merge protocol defined precisely.
